subject: Next steps: Dev onboarding & local quickstart (Python / TypeScript)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmecloud.com>; Ben Carter <ben.carter@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & quickstart options — Acme discovery call

Hi Sarah / Ben — great conversation this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we all have a single source of truth: 

Recap (from discovery)
- Primary use cases: relevance/reranking for search + structured extraction for customer support routing.
- Data residency: must be in customer VPC (private deployment) for initial POC; low-latency on queries required (~150ms p95 target).
- Auth: you currently prefer an OIDC-forwarded flow tied to your internal identity provider, but open to API-key for rapid POC.
- Success criteria: reproducible local dev loop, sample app with embeddings + reranker, and a short architecture review before any Dedicated commitment.

Immediate next steps I propose (please confirm):
1) Share a concise dev quickstart (Python + TypeScript) you can run locally against a sandbox account — I attached a zip with sample apps we can iterate on.
2) Marissa to provide SDK snippets and a recommended local env checklist (env vars, token/caching suggestions, minimal Docker for local emulation).
3) Schedule a 60-min architecture walkthrough with your infra team to validate VPC routing, ingress, and fallback policies (propose Wed 3/24 or Thu 3/25).
4) Mutual action plan and timeline: we draft a one-pager and finalize the POC acceptance criteria.

Questions for you now:
- Do you want the quickstart to use API key auth for the POC, or should we wire an OIDC flow from day one?
- Which sample should we prioritize first: embeddings + reranker demo, or tool-calling/structured output for ticket triage?

Attaching: redwood_dev_quickstart_v1.zip (sample apps + instructions), sketch of a recommended routing path (arch_routing_sketch.svg).

Thanks — I’ll hold off on the account setup until I get your preference on auth.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>; Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up & quickstart options — Acme discovery call

Thanks Rishi — attaching the Quickstart package and a short README in the repo link. High-level notes from my side (quickstart + local testing):

What’s included in redwood_dev_quickstart_v1.zip
- sample_apps/python_embed_rerank/  -> minimal Python app: create embeddings, index locally (sqlite), basic reranker scoring.
- sample_apps/ts_toolcall/ -> Node/TS example showing function/tool calling (mock external tool).
- docker/local-inference.md -> steps to run a lightweight container that simulates request routing and caching for local latency tests.
- sample_apps-readme.md -> runbook + env checklist.

Minimal env & auth options (choose one for POC)
- API_KEY (fast to get started): set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your env. Suitable for local dev and early demos.
- OIDC (recommended for production): we can demo the OIDC handshake; requires your IdP metadata and one-time setup in a private control plane.

Python quickstart (outline)
- pip install redwood==0.9.1
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=<>  # or export REDWOOD_OIDC_CLIENT_ID=...
- python sample_apps/python_embed_rerank/run_demo.py

Node/TypeScript quickstart (outline)
- npm install @redwood/inference@0.9.1
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=<>
- cd sample_apps/ts_toolcall && npm run start

Routing & structured output notes
- For your routing requirement (low latency p95), we recommend: prefix caching for hot queries, a dedicated small pool for the POC model, and a fallback policy to a cheaper model if capacity spikes. See arch_routing_sketch.svg (attached).
- Tool calling example (TS) in sample_apps/ts_toolcall demonstrates how to declare a tool interface and parse structured JSON responses safely. It also includes a small test harness that asserts output shape for CI.

Local testing tips
- Use the docker/local-inference image to validate latency under contended CPU. Keep sequence lengths short in the POC (<=256) to hit your p95 target.
- We include a small script to simulate a 5-user concurrent workload (scripts/loadtest.sh).

Next actions I can take this week
- Prepare a tailored sample that wires into your IdP test tenant for OIDC (needs metadata).
- Prep an architecture runbook for the walkthrough.

If you want, I can jump on a quick 30-min call with your infra engineer to walk through the repo end-to-end.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmecloud.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up & quickstart options — Acme discovery call

Thanks Rishi / Marissa — this looks great and very actionable. Quick replies / clarifications from our side: 

1) For the POC we prefer API_KEY to get started (faster) but we will want OIDC for any integration beyond the sandbox. Please include both flows in the repo if it’s not too much work.
2) Prioritize the embeddings + reranker sample first — that’s the lowest lift for our product team to evaluate relevance improvements.
3) A TS example for tool calling would be helpful; specifically, do you have an example that integrates with our ticketing system webhook (we use internal HTTP POST shape)? We’d like to see how Redwood signals structured output and how we can validate it server-side.

Scheduling: Wed 3/24 10:00 AM PT would work for our infra lead (Alex Kim). Can you confirm and send a calendar invite?

Thanks — looping Ben to confirm timelines; we aim to have the POC running in your sandbox within two weeks if nothing blocks.

—Sarah
